test_title: PYST 21: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: To promote agricultural exports and global competitiveness, reforms were extended to the agricultural sector as well. Which of the following initiatives aims to create a seamless national market for agricultural commodities?
solution:
The correct answer is __**e-NAM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **e-NAM (National Agriculture Market)** is a pan-India electronic trading platform launched by the **Government of India on April 14, 2016**, under the Ministry of Agriculture.
 
• The platform aims to integrate agricultural markets across the country, providing farmers with better price discovery and reducing the need for middlemen.
 
• e-NAM facilitates online trading of agricultural commodities, enabling farmers to sell their produce directly to buyers in a transparent manner.
 
• It connects existing Agricultural Produce Market Committees (APMCs) and other market yards into a unified network, ensuring a seamless national market for agricultural commodities.
 
• As of 2023, e-NAM has onboarded more than 1,000 mandis (markets) across India, significantly improving market access for farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC) Act**

 
 
• The APMC Act governs the sale of agricultural produce in regulated markets (mandis).
 
• It aims to prevent exploitation of farmers by intermediaries but has been criticized for creating inefficiencies and limiting farmers' ability to sell freely.
 
• Many states have amended the APMC Act to allow direct marketing, contract farming, and private market establishment.
 
 
 
• **PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)**
 
 
• Launched in February 2019, PM-KISAN provides direct income support of ₹6,000 per year to small and marginal farmers.
 
• The amount is paid in three equal installments of ₹2,000 each.
 
• This scheme aims to ensure financial stability for farmers and improve agricultural productivity.
 
 
 
• **Kisan Credit Card (KCC)**
 
 
• Introduced in 1998 by NABARD, the Kisan Credit Card scheme provides farmers with timely access to credit for agricultural and allied activities.
 
• It offers flexible repayment options and ensures liquidity for farmers during crucial farming periods.
 
 
 
• **e-NAM Features**
 
 
• Allows farmers to check real-time commodity prices and sell their produce at the best available rates.
 
• Facilitates payment directly to farmers' bank accounts, reducing delays and corruption.
 
• Promotes transparency and efficiency in agricultural trade by reducing market inefficiencies.
 
 

1a
